reviewScope: DR-125 component-sdk-contract v3 only. This review does not mark DR-125 SATISFIED, mint an owner grant, choose an SDK API, authorize docs/v2/implementation/, or apply or seal the candidate.
summary: REJECT. V3 removes the J-1 translation exception, conditions deadline fanout on the applied provider contract, orders provider Cancel before CPC teardown, and deletes the invented cancellation-equivalent death trigger. It remains non-applying, chooses no SDK API, mints no D9/exit or owner grant, and makes no SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, or implementation claim. Three defects bar acceptance. CSCV3-B1 makes the death event both appended and followed by a J-5 ladder even though CPC requires drain-before-death and death last. CSCV3-B2 separates eligibility sampling from Cancel commit without a linearization rule or failed-commit branch, leaving cancellation-versus-terminal and broken-write executions undefined. CSCV3-S1 finds /reMeasurementAtV3 outside the claimed closed v2-to-v3 roster. At 2 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, DR-125 remains OPEN and this verdict authorizes nothing.

blockers.title: The process-death repair starts the teardown ladder after the ladder's terminal event
blockers.measurement: V3 says that on host-observed process death the control plane 'appends the death boundary event and runs the teardown ladder.' CPC J-3 requires every channel to be drained to EOF before death is appended and makes death the LAST event in the child's merged order. CPC J-5 defines the one-way ladder as shutdown/cancel -> bounded wait -> EOF/drain -> kill -> reap/final death; every transition is appended and the ladder never skips backward. Starting or continuing that ladder after appending death necessarily creates events after the event CPC makes final, while attempting its shutdown/cancel/kill steps against an already-dead process is not a valid transition.
blockers.counterexample: A child dies spontaneously while no teardown is active. The v3 sentence permits appending death immediately and then issuing the ladder's shutdown/cancel and drain steps. That violates J-3's drain-before-death and death-last invariants. If 'runs the ladder' is instead read as occurring first, a spontaneous already-observed death cannot traverse T-1 through T-4, and the clause still supplies no lawful ordering.
blockers.whyBlocker: This is the core death branch of the proposed cancellation composition and directly contradicts the accepted CPC ordering while the artifact claims not to rewrite DR-102. Removing the invented cancellation-equivalent label did not produce a valid terminal branch.
blockers.requiredRepair: Distinguish physical death observation from logical event append. On spontaneous death, perform J-3 bounded channel drain and append the death event last; do not start a new J-5 ladder against a dead child. If a ladder is already active, state that the drained/reaped death completes its T-5 terminal step. Send no in-band Cancel, and leave fate/D9/exit meaning to the owning contracts.

blockers.title: Eligibility sampling and Cancel commit are not linearized and the transition relation has no commit-failure branch
blockers.measurement: The relation samples provider eligibility and then separately commands 'Commit ... FIRST,' but it supplies no linearization rule against a concurrent provider terminal frame and no branch for an admissible transition whose pipe write/commit fails. ifNotAdmissible covers only the sampled precondition; it does not cover failure after an admissible sample. The applied TypeScript contract permits Cancel only from a nonterminal state and only once, while CPC expressly requires hostile cancellation-versus-result races. G20 remains the unchanged generic phrase 'supervision cancel vs in-band Cancel' and carries no oracle for the sample/terminal race or failed commit.
counterexamples: The provider-side participant samples ANALYZING as Cancel-admissible. Before it commits Cancel, Complete arrives and terminalizes the provider protocol. Sending Cancel now violates the applied transition; suppressing it violates the v3 ifAdmissible branch. No v3 rule chooses the outcome.

The state and cause are admissible, but the request pipe closes during the write. The provider Cancel did not commit, so 'Then emit CPC supervision teardown' has no satisfied predecessor. V3 defines neither a CPC-progress fallback nor the owning fault event, allowing teardown to stall.
blockers.whyBlocker: A two-branch precondition test is not a total host-event transition relation when the checked state can race and the commanded transition can fail. This is exactly the reachability/failure hole CSCV2-B1 required the successor to close; notFoldedThisSuccessor is therefore false on the merits.
blockers.requiredRepair: Give the provider-side participant a behavioral linearization point that atomically validates the cause/state and commits or rejects the outbound Cancel relative to provider terminal events, without choosing an SDK API. Add an explicit commit-failed branch that proceeds to CPC supervision teardown and records the failure only under the owning provider/CPC contracts. Add G20 expected traces for terminal-wins, Cancel-wins, write-fails, already-terminal/already-cancelled, and no-in-band cases. Mint no frame, fate, D9/exit, API, or owner grant.
